userStories.title: Guard release tag targets, allow failed-push retries, and cover release inputs in CI
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make release tagging refuse commits other than origin/main, retry an undelivered local tag at HEAD, and ensure ordinary CI includes release action and patch inputs.

**Motivation** — After one local-only commit to a package source file, the CLI exited 0 again, and the remote tag held that commit while remote `main` still pointed at its parent.

**Approach** — Implement these Target instructions, not the baseline.

`tagRelease(dryRun)` (`packages/repo-tooling/scripts/release.ts`). Target, in this order:
1. `requireCleanMain()` and the shared version, as today.
2. Local tag check, with no network call. `git tag --list <tag>` tells whether the local tag exists; only when it does, `git rev-list -n 1 <tag>` gives its commit. (The `git()` helper throws on any non-zero exit, so a probe that exits 1 for a missing tag must not be used uncaught.) If the tag exists and its commit is not `git rev-parse HEAD`, throw `Tag <tag> already exists at <sha>, not at HEAD`.
3. Print the plan line. On `--dry-run`, return. No network call happens before this point or on a declined confirmation.
4. `confirm(...)`, unchanged. A declined confirmation prints `Aborted.` and returns.
5. Remote check, after confirmation: `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main refs/tags/<tag>`. `ls-remote` patterns match ref-name suffixes, so the output is read by exact ref name: only a line whose ref is exactly `refs/heads/main` or exactly `refs/tags/<tag>` counts. If the output has the `refs/tags/<tag>` line, throw `Tag <tag> already exists on origin`. If `refs/heads/main` is missing, or its commit is not `HEAD`, throw `Local main <head> does not match origin/main <remote>; pull or push main before tagging`. A failing `ls-remote` throws its error. In each case nothing is tagged or pushed.
6. Create the tag only when step 2 found none, then `git("push", "origin", tag)`. When step 2 found the tag at `HEAD`, skip `git tag` and push the existing tag.

`release.ts` is 206 lines. Keep the checks in `release.ts`. If the project's function-size limits force a helper into a new `packages/repo-tooling/scripts/lib/` file, `makeReleaseCliFixture` must also copy that file, because the fixture runs a copy of `release.ts` with only the files it lists (see Modifies).

`RELEASING.md`, the `bun run release tag` section. Target: one sentence says that after a failed tag push, rerunning `bun run release tag` on the same clean `main` pushes the existing local tag, and that the command refuses when local `main` differs from `origin/main`.

`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `on.push.paths` and `on.pull_request.paths`. Target: both lists also hold `.github/actions/**` and `patches/**`.

Integration — symbols this feature only reads:
- `packages/repo-tooling/scripts/release.ts`: `git(...args)`, `requireCleanMain()`, `sharedVersion(manifests)`, `confirm(message)`, `distTagsFor(version)`. `bumpRelease` and its `rejectExistingTag(plan.tag)` call are unchanged.
- `packages/repo-tooling/test/helpers/release-cli-fixture.ts`: `makeReleaseCliFixture()`. It returns `{ dir, git, write, run(args, input?, env?) }`. `run` puts stub `git`/`bun`/`gh` scripts first on `PATH`. The `git` stub fakes `pull` and `push` (`exit ${FAIL_PUSH:-0}`) and passes every other subcommand to `/usr/bin/git`. Passing `{ PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" }` as `env` replaces the stubs with real git, which is how the review proof pushed to a bare remote.
- `packages/repo-tooling/test/helpers/release-shell.ts`: loads workflow YAML with `Bun.YAML.parse(readFileSync(new URL(".github/workflows/release.yml", REPO), "utf8"))`. The CI-paths test loads `ci.yml`, `release.yml` and the root `package.json` the same way, and matches paths against the `paths` globs with `Bun.Glob`, as the review proof did.

Required fixture modification — `packages/repo-tooling/test/helpers/release-cli-fixture.ts`: the fixture repository has no `origin` remote, so the new post-confirmation `git ls-remote origin` fails every confirmed `tag` run. After the fixture commit, the fixture creates a bare repository named origin.git inside its temp directory, adds /origin.git/ to the same single write that sets the repository's info/exclude entries for the stub directory and logs, or appends it after that write, never before it, because that write replaces the file (so `requireCleanMain` still sees a clean tree, and `cleanupTempDir(dir)` still removes everything), adds it as `origin`, and seeds it with the fixture's `main` through the real git binary (never the stub). If the release script imports a new scripts/lib file, the fixture's copy list gains that file. The invariant: in a fresh fixture, origin's main equals the local `HEAD`, `origin` holds no tags, the stubbed `push` still records calls, and the fixture tree stays clean.

Existing test modification — `packages/repo-tooling/test/unit/release/release-cli.test.ts`: the `existing-tag` case of `tag rejects a %s checkout before creating or pushing a tag` creates `v0.84.0` at `HEAD`, which is now the retry case and pushes. The invariant becomes: the case tags `HEAD`, then adds one more commit so the tag points at a commit other than `HEAD`, and `tag` still exits non-zero with no `git push` or `git tag v` call.

Failure handling:
- `git ls-remote origin` fails (no `origin`, network error): The error propagates and the CLI exits 1. Nothing is tagged or pushed.
- `origin` has no `main` branch: Refused with the `does not match origin/main` error. Nothing is tagged or pushed.
- The tag push fails after the local tag was created: Exits 1, as today. The local tag stays at `HEAD`, so a rerun pushes it.

Test setup: use `makeReleaseCliFixture()` with its bare `origin`. Run `tag` with real git using `run(["tag"], "y\n", { PATH: "/usr/bin:/bin" })`; inspect origin refs by running git rev-parse inside the bare repository. Create `release-tag-remote.test.ts` for real-git behavior and `ci-paths.test.ts` for dynamically derived CI inputs. Existing control cases must remain passing.

**Scope** — In: release tag checks/retry, CLI error output and exit status, fixture adaptation, the existing mismatching-local-tag test, root CI filters, dynamic release-input invariant, and the retry sentence. Out: US-002's model-map detection and calendar validation. Relevant feature boundaries:
- US-001 only: `bun run release --dry-run tag` and a declined confirmation make no network call; the remote checks run only after the push is confirmed.
- US-001 only: the bump path (`bun run release <canary|promote|patch|minor|major|X.Y.Z>`) is unchanged; it already pulls with `--ff-only` and re-checks the release inputs.
- US-001 only: release tags stay lightweight; annotated or signed tags are not introduced.
- US-001 only: a remote tag that already exists is refused even when it points at `HEAD`; the CLI does not report it as delivered.
- US-001 only: the tag-time gates in `.github/workflows/release.yml` are unchanged.
- US-001 only: the `RELEASING.md` retry sentence is a documentation change that no test verifies.
- US-001 only: the CI-paths invariant covers the local actions that `release.yml` steps use and the root `package.json` `patchedDependencies` files; other files that workflows reference are not enumerated.

**Interface** — Existing private entry point: `async function tagRelease(dryRun: boolean): Promise<void>`. Existing CLI: `bun run release [--dry-run] tag`. No new exported symbol or seam. Public test entry point remains `makeReleaseCliFixture()` returning `{ dir, git, write, run(args, input?, env?) }`.

userStories.title: Accept model/provider tier names and reject impossible schedule dates
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Narrow legacy model-map detection to actual definition shapes and reject impossible ISO calendar components before JavaScript Date normalization.

**Motivation** — With the tier renamed `model` or `provider`, it exited 1 with `Invalid configuration`.

**Approach** — Implement these Target instructions, not the baseline.

`isLegacyFlatModels(val)` (`packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts`). Target: returns `true` when any top-level value is a string, or a non-null object whose `provider` and `model` are both strings. An object holding only one of them, or holding a non-string `model` or `provider` (a tier mapped to a model definition object), does not count as legacy. The doc comment states the new rule.

`parseIso(input, now)` (`packages/nax/src/schedule/parse.ts`). Target: before building the date, any input matching the naive or offset form has its leading `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM(:SS)?` checked. The month must be 1-12. The day must be from 1 to the number of days in that month of that year under the Gregorian leap rule (divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400). The hour must be 0-23, and the minute and second 0-59. When a component is out of range, return `{ ok: false, error: `Schedule "${input}" names a date or time that does not exist.` }`. Valid inputs take today's path unchanged. An input that matches neither form keeps today's path too, ending in the `Unrecognized schedule` error. An input that matches the offset form but does not start with `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` also skips the calendar check and keeps today's path.

Integration — symbols this feature only reads:
- `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts`: `ModelDefSchema` (`provider` and `model` required non-empty strings), `TierMapSchema`, `PerAgentModelMapSchema`.
- `packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts`: `loadConfig(startDir?, cliOverrides?)`. Its tests isolate the global layer with `NAX_GLOBAL_CONFIG_DIR` and `_clearRootConfigCache()` (`test/unit/config/loader-mcp-literal.test.ts`).
- `packages/nax/src/schedule/parse.ts`: `resolveScheduleGate(input, now)`, which `resolveRunScheduleAndPlanFlags` in `packages/nax/bin/run-action.ts` calls before any setup. Unchanged.

Failure handling:
- A tier map value is an object holding only `provider` (no `model`): Read as a per-agent tier map. Before this feature it was migrated as legacy and then failed `ModelDefSchema`.
- A schedule names a nonexistent date or time: `parseSchedule` and `resolveScheduleGate` return `ok: false` with the `does not exist` error. `nax run --schedule` prints `Invalid --schedule: ...` and exits 1, as for any rejected value.

Create `packages/nax/test/unit/config/model-map-tier-names.test.ts` for the `model` and `provider` tier-name tests, using `NaxConfigSchema.safeParse(baseConfig(models))` with the helper shape in `test/unit/config/schemas.test.ts`, plus the isolated `loadConfig` proof. Create `packages/nax/test/unit/schedule/parse-calendar.test.ts` for the impossible-date tests. Existing tests need no modification: The existing legacy-migration tests use values with both `provider` and `model`, or string values, which stay legacy. The existing schedule tests use dates that exist. Native model ids must be written `provider/model`, per `validateNativeModelIds`. For schedule ACs use `now = new Date(2026, 0, 1, 0, 0, 0)`. Verify local date components for naive controls and UTC epoch milliseconds for the Z control. Test private changes through existing production entry points; no exported helper or seam is added.

**Scope** — In: the legacy predicate and doc comment, ISO calendar validation, schema/loadConfig regressions, parseSchedule/resolveScheduleGate regressions. CLI wiring is unchanged. Out: US-001's release tagging, retries, release documentation and CI inputs. Relevant feature boundaries:
- US-002 only: a per-agent tier map whose tiers are `provider` and `model`, both with string values, is still read as one legacy model definition, because that shape cannot be told apart from a legacy entry.
- US-002 only: a model map that mixes a legacy model definition with a per-agent entry is migrated as legacy, as today.
- US-002 only: a naive local time inside a daylight-saving gap keeps today's behaviour, where the platform shifts it.
- US-002 only: the range of an explicit UTC offset (for example `+25:00`) is not newly validated.

**Interface** — Existing signatures remain `function isLegacyFlatModels(val: unknown): boolean`, `function parseIso(input: string, now: Date): ScheduleParseResult`, `export function parseSchedule(input: string, now: Date): ScheduleParseResult`, and `export function resolveScheduleGate(input: string | undefined, now: Date): ScheduleGateResult`. Existing schedule result behavior is `{ ok: false, error: string }` on rejection and `{ ok: true, target: Date }` on a parsed date; the gate retains its undefined-input behavior. No public API change.

analysis:
This is a targeted enhancement of existing release tooling and two existing nax validation paths, not a greenfield project. Codebase-memory MCP was unavailable in this tool set; direct reads and text search were used instead. The binding decomposition is exactly US-001 in packages/repo-tooling and US-002 in packages/nax, both independent. All paths below are repository-root relative, including root workflow/documentation edits owned by US-001 despite its required package workdir.

US-001 findings and impact: package.json:11 routes the root release command to packages/repo-tooling/scripts/release.ts. That script's git helper uses execFileSync and throws for nonzero statuses (release.ts:43-45); requireCleanMain checks the branch and porcelain status (release.ts:47-50). rejectExistingTag at release.ts:52-54 is also used by bumpRelease at release.ts:152 and must remain unchanged for that path. The current tagRelease at release.ts:170-190 rejects any local tag, returns for dry-run or declined confirmation, then creates and pushes a lightweight tag without querying origin. sharedVersion at release.ts:69-73 retains lockstep enforcement; the main catch at release.ts:203-206 prints the error and sets exit code 1. Modify tagRelease and, if needed, small private helpers in the same file; no exported API or dependency is needed. The safe order is local clean-main/version/tag-target inspection, plan, dry-run return, confirmation/decline return, one exact-ref-parsed ls-remote, then conditional local tag creation and push. An origin query must never happen before confirmation. A matching local tag is a retry candidate, not proof of remote delivery. Remote tag existence always wins over main matching and must refuse without mutation. A failed remote query or missing main must not leave a new local tag; a failed push intentionally does. Parsing ls-remote by suffix is unsafe because patterns match ref-name suffixes: compare the complete ref name. Remote checks are a point-in-time guard, not a new distributed locking protocol.

The existing fixture copies release.ts and an explicit list of lib dependencies (packages/repo-tooling/test/helpers/release-cli-fixture.ts:50-57); a new imported file would require extending that list, so prefer keeping checks in release.ts. Its git method already invokes /usr/bin/git (release-cli-fixture.ts:75-76), whereas run normally prepends stubs and the push stub does not mutate origin (release-cli-fixture.ts:19-24, 101-109). Passing PATH=/usr/bin:/bin uses real git while the release script still runs via process.execPath (release-cli-fixture.ts:94-109). Seed a bare origin.git under the fixture temp root after the initial commit (release-cli-fixture.ts:77-82), using real git, with main at HEAD and no tags. The single overwrite of .git/info/exclude at release-cli-fixture.ts:91 must include /origin.git/ or be followed by an append; an earlier append is lost and makes requireCleanMain fail. Keep stub logging and FAIL_PUSH behavior intact. Tests must inspect real bare-remote refs instead of interpreting a stubbed successful push as delivery. Additional commits and a second clone for remote-ahead tests need temp cleanup and must not dirty the primary fixture checkout accidentally. Existing release-cli.test.ts:106-119 tags HEAD for its existing-tag case; add a later commit so that case still represents a mismatching tag. The confirmed tag control at release-cli.test.ts:122-127 should continue to record the stubbed push, and bump tests at release-cli.test.ts:35-74 must not change behavior. New release-tag-remote.test.ts owns real-remote proofs; release-cli.test.ts still provides existing dry-run, clean-tree, branch, bump and call-order controls.

CI push and pull_request filters currently omit both action and patch paths (.github/workflows/ci.yml:4-24). Add .github/actions/** and patches/** to each list only. release.yml checks out the tag at .github/workflows/release.yml:33-35 and invokes the local publish composite in every publishing job (release.yml:70, 86, 102, 118), which is why tagging an unmerged local commit can publish unreviewed code. Root package.json:16-18 declares the ink patch input. Follow packages/repo-tooling/test/helpers/release-shell.ts:25-34 for repository-relative YAML loading with Bun.YAML.parse and readFileSync, and use Bun.Glob to match root-relative release inputs against each CI event's actual path list. Derive local action directories from every job's step uses values beginning ./ and derive patch filenames from patchedDependencies values, rather than hard-coding today's publish action or ink patch. Include release.yml and package.json as existing matched controls. Do not extend the invariant to all workflow-referenced files or modify release.yml. Update RELEASING.md:28-52 with the pre-delivery tag retry and main-alignment sentence; its existing workflow retry concerns already-delivered tags and is not the same operation. No release, version bump, npm publication or real production remote mutation is part of implementation or verification.

US-002 findings and impact: packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts:266-276 defines ModelDefSchema with nonempty provider/model strings; ModelEntrySchema is at :278, the overly broad private isLegacyFlatModels at :281-289, tier validation at :292-303, and ModelMapSchema preprocessing into claude at :305-310. Change only the private detection predicate and its comment: string values still trigger migration; an object triggers only when both fields are strings. Do not replace this shape check with ModelDefSchema.safeParse, since nonemptiness and other schema validation remain later responsibilities. ModelMapSchema is consumed by NaxConfigSchema (packages/nax/src/config/schemas.ts:57,122), which also feeds defaults and the loader. Root loader validation uses that same schema after alias expansion (packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:225); loadConfig is at :250 and _clearRootConfigCache at :318. Package-layer validation also uses NaxConfigSchema (packages/nax/src/config/package-layer.ts:266), so the predicate fix naturally reaches multiple entry points without loader changes. Native model IDs are further checked at packages/nax/src/config/schemas-protocol-gate.ts:113-135, so new native fixtures must use openai/one even when an object has a separate provider field.
